messages:
john_acme: Hey team, we're seeing a streaming inference call from our product drop mid-response. Client gets a truncated final chunk and our side sees a 502/5xx from Redwood, which then counted as a server error in billing. Can we get a quick check? Request id: req-9b3f. Happened ~3 times in last hour.

alex_support: sorry about that, @john_acme. Can you paste the curl you used and confirm if you went through our hosted API (api.redwood.ai) or a private deployment? Also any proxy in front of your client? :thinking_face: 

john_acme: We're on hosted (api.redwood.ai). No custom proxy, but the frontend (Vercel edge) streams the response to the browser. curl we used for repro:

```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"model": "open-xxl", "prompt": "<very long prompt>"}' -H "X-Request-ID: req-9b3f"
```
\nIt seems to stream a few hundred tokens then suddenly the connection ends with 'broken pipe' on our end. We were billed for full token cost but only got partial output.

alex_support: thanks. Can you also share any response headers you captured and whether the browser reported `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` or similar? We need to know if the upstream closed or the client.

john_acme: Browser console shows `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`. No extra headers captured besides `content-type: text/event-stream` and `transfer-encoding: chunked`.

oncall-bot: New trace attached: trace/req-9b3f (edge->gateway->runtime).

erica_infra: I pulled the trace. Gateway returned a 502 because the runtime TCP connection reset while streaming. Upstream logs show `write: connection reset by peer` on the runtime side at the same time. Hypothesis: LB idle timeout/FIN race between edge and runtime.

kyle_eng: curious — is the reset originating from client (browser) or runtime? The trace shows `RST` sequence from the client IP (X-forwarded-for: 52.12.34.56). But the gateway's classification code marks any upstream reset as 5xx. That causes billing to treat it as server error. We should differentiate client-initiated resets vs runtime fault.

alex_support: @maya_billing can you hold any charge for req-9b3f until we confirm? Customer is disputing.

maya_billing: pausing charges for the req-9b3f session and flagging for manual review. Please supply a root cause so we can decide refund.

john_acme: I can repro consistently if I stream via our app (browser). If I use curl directly from my laptop it completes fine. 

erica_infra: that nails it — likely something in the edge (Vercel) or the browser's connection to the edge is dropping. The gateway sees the client close the connection mid-stream which results in the runtime receiving a broken pipe when it tries to write. From runtime's POV that's an error. We currently count that as a 5xx.

kyle_eng: action items: (1) add metric to distinguish `upstream_write_failed_due_to_client_close` vs `upstream_write_failed_due_to_runtime` (2) change billing classification to not mark token usage as server 5xx when the client initiated the close and at least one chunk was delivered (3) add an event log for request id to help support. I'll spin up a quick patch for metrics.

alex_support: For short-term mitigation, could the customer set `Connection: keep-alive` or reduce chunk buffer frequency? Any recommended client-side change to avoid this?

erica_infra: If the edge (Vercel) is buffering and then force-closing idle connections, increasing the keep-alive or sending a small noop chunk every 15s helps. Example: server-sent-event heartbeat `:\n` heartbeat sent periodically. Also client should avoid large single chunks until we fix classification.

john_acme: thanks — we'll try heartbeat. Can you share a quick repro script we can run from a browser environment to simulate?

kyle_eng: here's a minimal JS snippet to stream and send a heartbeat from the edge to keep connections alive: 

```
// fetch streaming SSE and ping every 12s
const es = new EventSource('/proxy-stream?rid=req-9b3f');
es.onmessage = (m) => console.log(m.data);
setInterval(() => fetch('/proxy-ping?rid=req-9b3f'), 12000);
```
Not ideal, but should reduce FIN races.

alex_support: @john_acme can you confirm after trying the heartbeat whether you still see truncated payloads? If it persists, please attach the browser HAR and the X-Request-ID.

john_acme: Will do. One more observation: the logs show a late EOF — response finishes but client connection already closed, then runtime logs `SIGPIPE` when writing trailing chunk. Could that be a server bug?

kyle_eng: possible but lower probability given curl success. I think it's client-edge path. We'll keep digging. If we can reproduce with a simple headless Chromium in CI that will prove edge involvement. I'll create a quick CI job to reproduce across different network paths.

maya_billing: holding the credit until root cause confirmed. If we determine client-edge caused it, we'll offer goodwill credit for the interrupted session but not a full refund.

alex_support: thanks everyone. Next steps: @john_acme try heartbeat and attach HAR + any browser error. @kyle_eng and @erica_infra to add metric patch and run CI repro. I'll follow up with customer within 1 business hour. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: CI repro job queued: job/stream-eof-repro-205678.

kyle_eng: created metric PR to tag `client_closed_before_runtime_finish` in traces, linking to trace ids. Will link PR here when ready.

john_acme: heartbeat worked for one run — no truncation. We'll run more and report. Thanks for the fast help! :relieved:
